intro: Welcome! Today you learn to explain a problem clearly, complain politely and handle phone and video calls: the internet provider, an ojek online app, a parcel that never came, a hotel booking, a Zoom meeting. Warm-up: how do you start a phone call in English when you want to say 'Halo, saya Budi'?
teachingNotes: This is a functional lesson that builds on a2-routine-transactions (Excuse me + the problem + Could you …? / Could I have …? / I'd like …; doesn't work / isn't working; a refund; Here's my receipt) and b1-indirect-questions-tags (Could you tell me …? / Do you know if …?, tags to check). Recap those in a line; don't re-teach them. New here: explaining a problem in three parts (what · when · what you've tried), polite complaint openers and asking for a solution, and phone / video call language.

Explaining a problem: WHAT (The internet is down. / The app doesn't work. / My parcel hasn't arrived yet.), WHEN with the past simple and a finished time (It stopped working this morning. I ordered it last Monday.) or a short answer to 'Since when?' (Since this morning.), WHAT YOU'VE TRIED with the present perfect and no time word (I've restarted the router twice. I've already called the driver.). Trap from 'mati sejak tadi pagi': *'The internet is die since this morning' / *'It is not working since this morning' → 'It stopped working this morning.' The present perfect continuous (has been down since …) and for/since with the present perfect are NOT in this lesson's chain: if the learner asks, say it's a form for later and give the past simple version.

Complaining politely: a soft opener (I'm afraid there's a problem with …, I'd like to make a complaint about …, Sorry to bother you, but …), the facts calmly, then ONE request (Could you …, please?, I'd appreciate it if you could …, What can you do about it?). Traps: 'I'm afraid' here is not 'saya takut' but 'sayangnya / mohon maaf'; complain is the verb and a complaint the noun (*'I want to complaint'); 'I'd appreciate it if you could' needs it (*'I'd appreciate if you could') and is a phrase to remember (don't analyse would/could + if: the second conditional comes later). Too direct ('Change my room now!', 'You are wrong') and too indirect ('Sorry before, maybe, if possible …') are both shown as the wrong end of the scale.

Phone calls: the node's common error 'Hello, I am Budi. Can I speak with Mr Andi?' → 'Hello, this is Budi. Could I speak to Mr Andi, please?'. On the phone you say this is (or Budi speaking), not I am, because the other person can't see you. 'speak to' is the usual form in both British and American English; 'speak with' is also correct (more American), so don't mark it wrong on its own; the real fixes are this is and Could I … please?. When someone asks for you: Speaking. Other phrases: Who's calling, please?, Hold on (informal) / One moment, please (polite), I'll call you back (British also ring back), Can I take a message?, Could you ask him to call me back?

Video calls and bad lines: Can you hear me?, You're on mute (mic-mu mati), Sorry, you're breaking up (suaramu putus-putus), Could you say that again, please?, Could you spell that, please?. For spelling, remind the learner of English letter names where Indonesian differs: A = 'ei', E = 'ii', I = 'ai', G = 'ji', J = 'jei', Y = 'wai'. Listening questions use one voice: no speaker labels in listen text.

Limits: A0–A2 grammar plus indirect questions and tags. No passive (avoid 'it was delivered', 'I was charged': say 'the app says delivered', 'the app charged me twice'), no past perfect, no reported speech, no second conditional, no present perfect continuous, no 'Would you mind …'. British / American: mobile / cell phone, ring / call, Hang on (British, informal) / Hold on.

keyPoints.title: Explain a problem: what, when, what you've tried
keyPoints.explanation: Say what's wrong (The internet is down. My parcel hasn't arrived yet.), when it started with the past simple (It stopped working this morning.) and what you've tried with the present perfect (I've restarted the router twice.). Not 'It is not working since this morning'.

examples.en: The internet is down. It stopped working last night.
examples.id: Internetnya mati. Berhenti berfungsi tadi malam.

examples.en: I've restarted the router twice, but it still doesn't work.
examples.id: Saya sudah me-restart router dua kali, tapi tetap tidak bisa.

examples.en: My parcel hasn't arrived yet, but the app says 'delivered'.
examples.id: Paket saya belum sampai, tapi di aplikasi tertulis 'terkirim'.

id.title: Menjelaskan masalah: apa, kapan, apa yang sudah dicoba
id.explanation: Katakan apa masalahnya (The internet is down. My parcel hasn't arrived yet.), kapan mulainya dengan past simple (It stopped working this morning.) dan apa yang sudah kamu coba dengan present perfect (I've restarted the router twice.). Bukan 'It is not working since this morning'.

keyPoints.title: Complain politely and ask for a solution
keyPoints.explanation: Start softly (I'm afraid there's a problem with …, I'd like to make a complaint about …, Sorry to bother you, but …), give the facts calmly, then ask for one thing: Could you …, please?, I'd appreciate it if you could … (a phrase to remember) or What can you do about it?

examples.en: I'd like to make a complaint about my internet connection.
examples.id: Saya ingin menyampaikan komplain tentang koneksi internet saya.

examples.en: Sorry to bother you, but the app charged me twice.
examples.id: Maaf mengganggu, tapi aplikasinya memotong saldo saya dua kali.

examples.en: I'd appreciate it if you could check it today.
examples.id: Saya akan sangat berterima kasih kalau Anda bisa mengeceknya hari ini.

id.title: Komplain dengan sopan dan meminta solusi
id.explanation: Mulai dengan halus (I'm afraid there's a problem with … = mohon maaf, ada masalah dengan …; I'd like to make a complaint about …; Sorry to bother you, but …), sampaikan faktanya dengan tenang, lalu minta satu hal: Could you …, please?, I'd appreciate it if you could … (ungkapan untuk dihafal) atau What can you do about it?

keyPoints.title: Phone and video calls
keyPoints.explanation: On the phone, say Hello, this is Budi (not I am Budi) and Could I speak to Mr Andi, please?. Useful: Speaking (= saya sendiri), Hold on / One moment, please, I'll call you back. On video calls: Can you hear me?, You're on mute, Sorry, you're breaking up, Could you say that again / spell that, please?

examples.en: Good morning, this is Sari from PT Maju Jaya.
examples.id: Selamat pagi, saya Sari dari PT Maju Jaya.

examples.en: One moment, please. I'll put you through.
Sorry, you're breaking up. I'll call you back.
examples.id: Maaf, suaramu putus-putus. Nanti saya telepon balik.

id.title: Telepon dan video call
id.explanation: Di telepon, katakan Hello, this is Budi (bukan I am Budi) dan Could I speak to Mr Andi, please?. Ungkapan berguna: Speaking (= saya sendiri), Hold on / One moment, please (tunggu sebentar), I'll call you back (nanti saya telepon balik). Di video call: Can you hear me?, You're on mute, Sorry, you're breaking up, Could you say that again / spell that, please?

guidedPractice.hint: Lima hari yang lalu = five days …

guidedPractice.prompt: Tell the ojek online helpdesk what you've tried. Complete with one word: I've ___ restarted the app, but it still doesn't work.
guidedPractice.hint: Sudah = …, between have and the verb.

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete with one word: Good afternoon. I'd like to make a ___ about my delivery.
guidedPractice.hint: The noun, not the verb complain.

guidedPractice.prompt: On the phone, your friend's voice comes and goes. Complete with one word: Sorry, you're breaking ___.
The caller says a name you don't know. Ask how to write it. Complete with one word: Could you ___ that, please?

independentPractice.prompt: The ojek driver took a longer way and you paid more. You explained the problem to the helpdesk. Now ask for a solution with five words. Start with 'What can'.
expected: what can you do about it
what can you do about this
independentPractice.hint: What can + you + do + about + it?

independentPractice.prompt: A caller asks for your colleague Rina. She's at the next desk. Ask the caller politely to wait. Use two words + please.
The app doesn't work. The helpdesk asks: 'Since when?' It stopped working yesterday. Answer with two words.

assessment.prompt: Your home Wi-Fi was fine last night, but at seven this morning it suddenly went off. Tell the provider when the problem began. Complete with two words (use the verb stop): The Wi-Fi ___ ___ at seven this morning.
acceptableAnswers: stopped working
assessment.rubric: Correct: stopped working (past simple, because 'at seven this morning' is a finished time). 'stop working' = 50 (needs the past). 'has stopped working' = 50 (the present perfect doesn't go with a finished time). 'stopped' alone = 70. 'is stopped' / 'is not working' = 20.

assessment.prompt: The technician asks what you've done. You checked the cables before you called. Make one sentence with these words, using the present perfect: I / already / check / the cables
acceptableAnswers: i've already checked the cables
i have already checked the cables
ive already checked the cables
i've checked the cables already
i have checked the cables already
ive checked the cables already
assessment.rubric: Correct: I've (I have) already checked the cables. 'I already checked the cables' = 80 (fine in American English, but not the present perfect asked for). 'I have already check the cables' = 50 (have + third form: checked). 'I already check the cables' = 30.

assessment.prompt: You arrive at a hotel in Bali. You booked a room with two beds, but the receptionist gives you a room with one big bed. Start your complaint politely. Complete with one word: I'm afraid there's a ___ with my booking.
acceptableAnswers: problem
mistake
assessment.rubric: Correct: problem (mistake is also correct). 'trouble' = 60 (understood, but 'a problem with' is the phrase). 'wrong' = 20 (not a noun).

assessment.prompt: Your new rice cooker from an online shop arrived broken. You call the shop. Make this demand polite. Start with 'Could you': 'Send me a new one!'
acceptableAnswers: could you send me a new one please
could you send me a new one
could you please send me a new one
could you send a new one please
could you send a new one
could you send me another one please
could you send me another one
could you please send me another one
could you send me a replacement please
could you send me a replacement
could you please send me a replacement
could you send me a new rice cooker please
could you send me a new rice cooker
assessment.rubric: Correct: Could you send me a new one (another one, a replacement), please? Without please = 90. 'Could you send me new one' (no a) = 80. 'Could I send …' = 30 (that asks if YOU can send it). 'Send me a new one, please' = 40 (still an order, not the pattern asked).

assessment.prompt: Your hotel room is next to the lift and it's very noisy. Make this request softer. Start with 'I'd appreciate it if you could': Move me to another room.
acceptableAnswers: i'd appreciate it if you could move me to another room
id appreciate it if you could move me to another room
i would appreciate it if you could move me to another room
i'd appreciate it if you could move me to another room please
id appreciate it if you could move me to another room please
i would appreciate it if you could move me to another room please
assessment.rubric: Correct: I'd appreciate it if you could move me to another room. 'I'd appreciate if you could …' (no it) = 70. 'I'd appreciate it if you can …' = 70. 'I'd appreciate it if you could moved me …' = 50. Ending with please is fine.

assessment.prompt: You phone a client's office. The receptionist answers: 'Good morning, PT Sinar Abadi.' Your name is Dimas. Say who you are, the way people do on the phone. Start with 'Good morning,'.
acceptableAnswers: good morning this is dimas
good morning this is dimas speaking
good morning my name is dimas
good morning dimas speaking
good morning this is dimas here
assessment.rubric: Correct: Good morning, this is Dimas. ('Dimas speaking' and 'my name is Dimas' are also fine.) 'it's Dimas' = 80 (for someone who already knows you). 'I am Dimas' = 40 (the Indonesian 'saya Dimas' word for word; on the phone say this is). 'here is Dimas' = 30.

assessment.prompt: Listen to the receptionist. You want Pak Andi to phone you later. Complete with two words: Yes, please. Could you ask him to ___ me ___?
assessment.listen: Good afternoon, PT Maju Jaya. I'm sorry, Pak Andi is in a meeting right now. Can I take a message?
acceptableAnswers: call back
ring back
phone back
assessment.rubric: Correct: call … back (British also ring … back). 'call … later' = 70 (understood, but call back is the phrase). 'call … again' = 60. 'back … call' = 20.

material.title: Explain a problem: what, when, what you've tried

blocks.text:
When you call a helpdesk (the internet provider, an ojek online app, an online shop), the person can't see your problem. Help them with **three parts**:
- **What** is wrong: *The internet is **down**.* (down = mati, untuk internet/server) *The app **doesn't work**.* *My parcel **hasn't arrived yet**.*
- **When** it started: the **past simple** with a finished time: *It **stopped working** this morning.* *I **ordered** it last Monday.* If they ask *Since when?*, a short answer is enough: ***Since** this morning.*
- **What you've tried**: the **present perfect** (have/has + third form) with no time word, because it's what you've done up to now: *I**'ve restarted** the router twice.* *I**'ve already called** the driver.*

You know both tenses from A2. Here they work together: past simple for *when*, present perfect for *what you've tried*.

id.text:
Saat kamu menelepon layanan bantuan (provider internet, aplikasi ojek online, toko online), orangnya tidak bisa melihat masalahmu. Bantu dia dengan **tiga bagian**:
- **Apa** masalahnya: *The internet is **down**.* (down = mati, untuk internet/server) *The app **doesn't work**.* *My parcel **hasn't arrived yet**.* (paket saya belum sampai)
- **Kapan** mulainya: **past simple** dengan waktu yang sudah selesai: *It **stopped working** this morning.* (berhenti berfungsi tadi pagi) *I **ordered** it last Monday.* Kalau mereka bertanya *Since when?* (sejak kapan?), jawaban pendek sudah cukup: ***Since** this morning.*
- **Apa yang sudah kamu coba**: **present perfect** (have/has + bentuk ketiga) tanpa kata waktu, karena ini hal yang sudah kamu lakukan sampai sekarang: *I**'ve restarted** the router twice.* (sudah me-restart router dua kali) *I**'ve already called** the driver.*

Kedua tenses ini sudah kamu pelajari di A2. Di sini mereka bekerja sama: past simple untuk *kapan*, present perfect untuk *apa yang sudah dicoba*.

rows.en: The internet is down. It stopped working last night.
rows.id: Internetnya mati. Berhenti berfungsi tadi malam.

rows.en: I've restarted the router twice, but it still doesn't work.
rows.id: Saya sudah me-restart router dua kali, tapi tetap tidak bisa.

rows.en: My parcel hasn't arrived yet, but the app says 'delivered'.
rows.id: Paket saya belum sampai, tapi di aplikasi tertulis 'terkirim'.

rows.en: The app charged me twice for one trip.
rows.id: Aplikasinya memotong saldo saya dua kali untuk satu perjalanan.

blocks.text:
**The Indonesian trap:** *Internetnya mati dari tadi pagi* is not *'The internet is die since this morning'* or *'It is not working since this morning'*. Split it: say **what** (*The internet is down.*) and **when**, with the past simple: ***It stopped working this morning.*** (Another way, *has been down since*, uses a form you learn later.)

**Mati** has several English words: the internet or a website is **down**, a machine **doesn't work** / **is broken**, the power (listrik) is **off** (a power cut = mati lampu). *Die* is only for living things.

The present perfect never goes with a finished time: *I've restarted it **this morning*** ✗ → *I **restarted** it this morning* ✓ or *I**'ve restarted** it twice* ✓.

id.text:
**Jebakan bahasa Indonesia:** *Internetnya mati dari tadi pagi* bukan *'The internet is die since this morning'* atau *'It is not working since this morning'*. Pisahkan: katakan **apa** masalahnya (*The internet is down.*) dan **kapan**, dengan past simple: ***It stopped working this morning.*** (Cara lain, *has been down since*, memakai bentuk yang kamu pelajari nanti.)

**Mati** punya beberapa kata dalam bahasa Inggris: internet atau website **down**, mesin **doesn't work** / **is broken** (rusak), listrik **off** (mati lampu = a power cut). *Die* hanya untuk makhluk hidup.

Present perfect tidak pernah dipakai dengan waktu yang sudah selesai: *I've restarted it **this morning*** ✗ → *I **restarted** it this morning* ✓ atau *I**'ve restarted** it twice* ✓.

blocks.prompt: Your laptop doesn't turn on. The technician asks: 'When did the problem start?' It started on Saturday. Which answer is right?
options: It is not working since Saturday.
It has stopped working on Saturday.
blocks.explain: 'On Saturday' is a finished time, so use the past simple: It stopped working on Saturday. 'is not working since' is the word-for-word Indonesian 'sejak', and the present perfect (has stopped) can't go with a finished time.

id.prompt: Laptopmu tidak menyala. Teknisi bertanya: 'When did the problem start?' Masalahnya mulai hari Sabtu. Jawaban mana yang benar?
id.explain: 'On Saturday' adalah waktu yang sudah selesai, jadi pakai past simple: It stopped working on Saturday. 'is not working since' adalah terjemahan kata per kata dari 'sejak', dan present perfect (has stopped) tidak bisa dipakai dengan waktu yang sudah selesai.

id.title: Menjelaskan masalah: apa, kapan, apa yang sudah dicoba

material.title: Complain politely and ask for a solution

blocks.text:
In A2 you learnt the short recipe: *Excuse me* + the problem + *Could you …?* For a bigger problem, a complaint has **three steps**:
1. **A soft start:** ***I'm afraid** there's a problem with my order.* ***I'd like to make a complaint about** my internet connection.* ***Sorry to bother you, but** the driver didn't come.*
2. **The facts**, calmly: what, when, what you've tried.
3. **One clear request:** ***Could you** send a technician today, **please**?* ***I'd appreciate it if you could** check it today.* ***What can you do about it?***

**I'd appreciate it if you could …** (= saya akan sangat berterima kasih kalau Anda bisa …) is a **phrase to remember**: learn it as one block, with **it**. It's softer than *Could you …?* and good for emails and calls with companies.

id.text:
Di A2 kamu sudah belajar resep pendeknya: *Excuse me* + masalahnya + *Could you …?* Untuk masalah yang lebih besar, komplain punya **tiga langkah**:
1. **Pembuka yang halus:** ***I'm afraid** there's a problem with my order.* (mohon maaf, ada masalah dengan pesanan saya) ***I'd like to make a complaint about** my internet connection.* (saya ingin komplain tentang …) ***Sorry to bother you, but** the driver didn't come.* (maaf mengganggu, tapi …)
2. **Faktanya**, dengan tenang: apa, kapan, apa yang sudah dicoba.
3. **Satu permintaan yang jelas:** ***Could you** send a technician today, **please**?* ***I'd appreciate it if you could** check it today.* ***What can you do about it?*** (apa yang bisa Anda lakukan?)

**I'd appreciate it if you could …** (= saya akan sangat berterima kasih kalau Anda bisa …) adalah **ungkapan untuk dihafal**: pelajari sebagai satu blok, dengan **it**. Ungkapan ini lebih halus daripada *Could you …?* dan cocok untuk email dan telepon dengan perusahaan.

rows.en: Change my room now! This hotel is terrible!
rows.id: Ganti kamar saya sekarang! Hotel ini parah!

rows.en: Sorry before, sorry, maybe if possible, maybe the room …
rows.id: Mohon maaf sebelumnya, maaf, mungkin kalau bisa, mungkin kamarnya …
rows.note: too indirect: what is the problem?

rows.en: I'm afraid the air conditioner in my room isn't working. Could you send someone, please?
rows.id: Mohon maaf, AC di kamar saya tidak berfungsi. Bisa tolong kirim orang?
rows.note: just right: soft start + fact + request

rows.en: The technician didn't come yesterday. What can you do about it?
rows.id: Teknisinya kemarin tidak datang. Apa yang bisa Anda lakukan?

rows.en: I'd appreciate it if you could give me a refund.
rows.id: Saya akan sangat berterima kasih kalau Anda bisa mengembalikan uang saya.

blocks.text:
**I'm afraid** here doesn't mean *saya takut*. It means *sayangnya / mohon maaf, …*: a soft way to give bad news. *I'm afraid the food is cold.* = Mohon maaf, makanannya dingin.

**Complain or complaint?** **complain** is the verb (*I want to complain*), **a complaint** is the noun (*I'd like to make a complaint*). Not *'I want to complaint'*. In Indonesian *komplain* is both!

Say **I'd appreciate it if you could …**, not *'I'd appreciate if you could …'*: the **it** is needed.

Polite doesn't mean weak: say the facts clearly and ask for one thing. *You are wrong!* or *Your service is bad!* attack the person; *I'm afraid there's a mistake* talks about the problem.

id.text:
**I'm afraid** di sini bukan *saya takut*. Artinya *sayangnya / mohon maaf, …*: cara halus untuk menyampaikan kabar buruk. *I'm afraid the food is cold.* = Mohon maaf, makanannya dingin.

**Complain atau complaint?** **complain** adalah kata kerja (*I want to complain*), **a complaint** adalah kata benda (*I'd like to make a complaint*). Bukan *'I want to complaint'*. Dalam bahasa Indonesia *komplain* bisa dua-duanya!

Katakan **I'd appreciate it if you could …**, bukan *'I'd appreciate if you could …'*: **it**-nya wajib.

Sopan bukan berarti lemah: sampaikan faktanya dengan jelas dan minta satu hal. *You are wrong!* atau *Your service is bad!* menyerang orangnya; *I'm afraid there's a mistake* membicarakan masalahnya.

blocks.prompt: You paid for your ojek online trip in the app, but the driver asks you for cash. Which is polite AND clear?
options: I paid already! You are cheating me!
I'm afraid I've already paid in the app. Could you check your order, please?
Sorry before, maybe I pay already, maybe, if possible …
blocks.explain: A soft start (I'm afraid), the fact (I've already paid in the app) and one request (Could you check …, please?). The first one attacks the driver, and the third doesn't say the problem clearly.

id.prompt: Kamu sudah membayar perjalanan ojek online di aplikasi, tapi drivernya meminta uang tunai. Mana yang sopan DAN jelas?
id.explain: Pembuka yang halus (I'm afraid), faktanya (I've already paid in the app) dan satu permintaan (Could you check …, please?). Pilihan pertama menyerang drivernya, dan pilihan ketiga tidak menyampaikan masalahnya dengan jelas.

id.title: Komplain dengan sopan dan meminta solusi

material.title: On the phone: this is, not I am

blocks.text:
**Saying who you are.** On the phone, the other person can't see you, so English uses **this is** (= yang bicara ini): ***Hello, this is Budi.*** At work, add where you're from: *Good morning, this is Sari **from** PT Maju Jaya.* You can also say ***Budi speaking.*** Not *'I am Budi'*: that's the Indonesian *Saya Budi* word for word.

**Asking for someone:** ***Could I speak to** Mr Andi, **please**?*

**When they ask for you:** *Could I speak to Rina, please?* — ***Speaking.*** (= saya sendiri)

**Other useful phrases:**
- ***Who's calling, please?*** (dengan siapa ini?)
- ***Hold on.*** (informal) / ***One moment, please.*** (polite) = tunggu sebentar
- ***Can I take a message?*** (mau titip pesan?)
- ***I'll call you back.*** (nanti saya telepon balik) *call back* = telepon balik

id.text:
**Menyebutkan siapa kamu.** Di telepon, lawan bicaramu tidak bisa melihatmu, jadi bahasa Inggris memakai **this is** (= yang bicara ini): ***Hello, this is Budi.*** Di kantor, tambahkan asalmu: *Good morning, this is Sari **from** PT Maju Jaya.* Kamu juga bisa bilang ***Budi speaking.*** Bukan *'I am Budi'*: itu terjemahan kata per kata dari *Saya Budi*.

**Meminta bicara dengan seseorang:** ***Could I speak to** Mr Andi, **please**?* (bisa bicara dengan Pak Andi?)

**Kalau yang dicari kamu sendiri:** *Could I speak to Rina, please?* — ***Speaking.*** (= saya sendiri)

**Ungkapan berguna lainnya:**
- ***Who's calling, please?*** (dengan siapa ini?)
- ***Hold on.*** (santai) / ***One moment, please.*** (sopan) = tunggu sebentar
- ***Can I take a message?*** (mau titip pesan?)
- ***I'll call you back.*** (nanti saya telepon balik) *call back* = telepon balik

rows.en: Good morning, PT Maju Jaya. How can I help you?
rows.id: Selamat pagi, PT Maju Jaya. Ada yang bisa saya bantu?

rows.en: Good morning, this is Sari from Bank Sentosa. Could I speak to Pak Hasan, please?
rows.id: Selamat pagi, saya Sari dari Bank Sentosa. Bisa bicara dengan Pak Hasan?

rows.en: One moment, please. I'll put you through.
I'm sorry, he isn't at his desk. Can I take a message?
rows.id: Maaf, beliau sedang tidak di mejanya. Mau titip pesan?

rows.en: I'm driving right now. I'll call you back in ten minutes.
rows.id: Saya sedang menyetir. Sepuluh menit lagi saya telepon balik.

blocks.text:
**speak to or speak with?** *Could I speak to …?* is the most common, in British and American English. *speak with* is also correct (more American). The two real mistakes are *I am Budi* and a request without *Could … please* (*'I want to speak to Mr Andi'* sounds rude).

**British and American:** *ring* (British) = *call*: *I'll ring you back.* *Hang on* (British, informal) = *Hold on*. *mobile* (British) = *cell phone* (American).

**Mr or Pak?** With an Indonesian colleague, *Pak Andi* / *Bu Ani* is fine in English too. *Mr / Ms* go with the family name in English-speaking countries: *Mr Smith*.

id.text:
**speak to atau speak with?** *Could I speak to …?* paling umum, di bahasa Inggris British maupun Amerika. *speak with* juga benar (lebih Amerika). Dua kesalahan yang sebenarnya adalah *I am Budi* dan permintaan tanpa *Could … please* (*'I want to speak to Mr Andi'* terdengar kasar).

**British dan Amerika:** *ring* (British) = *call*: *I'll ring you back.* *Hang on* (British, santai) = *Hold on*. *mobile* (British) = *cell phone* (Amerika).

**Mr atau Pak?** Dengan rekan kerja orang Indonesia, *Pak Andi* / *Bu Ani* tetap boleh dalam bahasa Inggris. Di negara berbahasa Inggris, *Mr / Ms* dipakai dengan nama keluarga: *Mr Smith*.

blocks.prompt: Your phone rings. The caller says: 'Hello, could I speak to Rina, please?' You are Rina. What do you say?
blocks.explain: When the caller asks for you, the short answer is Speaking. (= saya sendiri). 'I am Rina here' is Indonesian word order, and 'I'm speaking' only says that you are talking.

id.prompt: Teleponmu berdering. Penelepon berkata: 'Hello, could I speak to Rina, please?' Kamu Rina. Apa jawabanmu?
id.explain: Kalau penelepon mencari kamu, jawaban pendeknya adalah Speaking. (= saya sendiri). 'I am Rina here' memakai urutan bahasa Indonesia, dan 'I'm speaking' hanya berarti kamu sedang bicara.

id.title: Di telepon: this is, bukan I am

blocks.text:
In a Zoom or Google Meet meeting, or on a bad phone line, these short sentences save the conversation:
- ***Can you hear me?*** (suara saya terdengar?)
- ***You're on mute.*** (mic-mu masih mati) *mute* = membisukan mikrofon; *unmute* = menyalakannya lagi.
- ***Sorry, you're breaking up.*** (maaf, suaramu putus-putus) The voice comes and goes.
- ***Could you say that again, please?*** (bisa diulang?)
- ***Could you spell that, please?*** (bisa dieja?) for names and email addresses.
- ***I'll call you back.*** when the line is really bad.

These are **Could you …?** requests, the same polite pattern as in a complaint.

id.text:
Di rapat Zoom atau Google Meet, atau saat sinyal telepon jelek, kalimat pendek ini menyelamatkan percakapan:
- ***Can you hear me?*** (suara saya terdengar?)
- ***You're on mute.*** (mic-mu masih mati) *mute* = membisukan mikrofon; *unmute* = menyalakannya lagi.
- ***Sorry, you're breaking up.*** (maaf, suaramu putus-putus) Suaranya hilang-timbul.
- ***Could you say that again, please?*** (bisa diulang?)
- ***Could you spell that, please?*** (bisa dieja?) untuk nama dan alamat email.
- ***I'll call you back.*** kalau sinyalnya benar-benar jelek.

Ini permintaan dengan **Could you …?**, pola sopan yang sama seperti saat komplain.

rows.en: Hi everyone. Can you hear me?
Budi, I think you're on mute.
Sorry, Rina, you're breaking up. Could you say that again, please?
rows.id: Maaf, Rina, suaramu putus-putus. Bisa diulang?

rows.en: My email is sari.lestari@gmail.com. — Could you spell that, please?

blocks.text:
**Spelling on the phone:** English letter names are different from Indonesian ones, and these are the ones people mix up: **A** = 'ei', **E** = 'ii', **I** = 'ai', **G** = 'ji', **J** = 'jei', **Y** = 'wai'. To make a letter clear, say **B for Bandung** or **B as in Budi**.

**You're on mute** is about the microphone; **you're breaking up** is about the connection. Don't say *'Your voice is broken'*: in English that sounds like your voice is damaged.

id.text:
**Mengeja di telepon:** nama huruf dalam bahasa Inggris berbeda dari bahasa Indonesia, dan huruf ini yang sering tertukar: **A** = 'ei', **E** = 'ii', **I** = 'ai', **G** = 'ji', **J** = 'jei', **Y** = 'wai'. Supaya hurufnya jelas, katakan **B for Bandung** atau **B as in Budi**.

**You're on mute** tentang mikrofon; **you're breaking up** tentang koneksi. Jangan bilang *'Your voice is broken'*: dalam bahasa Inggris itu terdengar seperti suaramu rusak.

blocks.prompt: In a Zoom meeting, Pak Hasan's voice comes and goes: you only hear some of his words. What do you say?
options: Sorry, Pak Hasan, you're breaking up. Could you say that again?
Sorry, Pak Hasan, you're on mute.
Pak Hasan, your voice is broken.
blocks.explain: A voice that comes and goes is breaking up, and you ask him to say it again. 'You're on mute' means you hear nothing at all, and 'your voice is broken' sounds like his voice is damaged.

id.prompt: Di rapat Zoom, suara Pak Hasan hilang-timbul: kamu hanya mendengar sebagian kata-katanya. Apa yang kamu katakan?
id.explain: Suara yang hilang-timbul = breaking up, lalu kamu minta beliau mengulanginya. 'You're on mute' berarti kamu sama sekali tidak mendengar apa-apa, dan 'your voice is broken' terdengar seperti suaranya rusak.

How do I say 'internetnya mati dari tadi pagi' in English?

id.intro: Selamat datang! Hari ini kamu belajar menjelaskan masalah dengan jelas, komplain dengan sopan, dan menangani telepon serta video call: provider internet, aplikasi ojek online, paket yang tidak pernah sampai, booking hotel, rapat Zoom. Pemanasan: bagaimana kamu memulai telepon dalam bahasa Inggris kalau ingin bilang 'Halo, saya Budi'?
suggestedQuestions: Kenapa di telepon aku bilang 'this is Budi', bukan 'I am Budi'?
Bagaimana bilang 'internetnya mati dari tadi pagi' dalam bahasa Inggris?

assessment.prc-1: Wi-Fi di rumahmu baik-baik saja tadi malam, tapi jam tujuh pagi ini tiba-tiba mati. Beri tahu provider kapan masalahnya mulai. Lengkapi dengan dua kata (pakai kata kerja stop): The Wi-Fi ___ ___ at seven this morning.
assessment.prc-2: Teknisi bertanya apa yang sudah kamu lakukan. Kamu sudah mengecek kabelnya sebelum menelepon. Buat satu kalimat bahasa Inggris dari kata-kata ini, dengan present perfect: I / already / check / the cables
assessment.prc-3: Kamu tiba di sebuah hotel di Bali. Kamu memesan kamar dengan dua tempat tidur, tapi resepsionis memberimu kamar dengan satu tempat tidur besar. Mulai komplainmu dengan sopan. Lengkapi dengan satu kata: I'm afraid there's a ___ with my booking.
assessment.prc-4: Rice cooker baru dari toko online datang dalam keadaan rusak. Kamu menelepon tokonya. Ubah tuntutan ini menjadi sopan, dalam bahasa Inggris. Mulai dengan 'Could you': 'Send me a new one!'
assessment.prc-5: Kamar hotelmu di sebelah lift dan sangat berisik. Buat permintaan ini lebih halus, dalam bahasa Inggris. Mulai dengan 'I'd appreciate it if you could': Move me to another room.
assessment.prc-6: Kamu menelepon kantor seorang klien. Resepsionis menjawab: 'Good morning, PT Sinar Abadi.' Namamu Dimas. Sebutkan siapa kamu dalam bahasa Inggris, seperti yang biasa dilakukan di telepon. Mulai dengan 'Good morning,'.
assessment.prc-7: Dengarkan resepsionisnya. Kamu ingin Pak Andi meneleponmu nanti. Lengkapi dengan dua kata: Yes, please. Could you ask him to ___ me ___?
